clue.text: Get at a can on the outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tin is placed around the letter A, so it sits on the outside of it

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Instructions for reaching something by going round the outside of a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' puts TIN around A to make TAIN, after AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to reach or achieve it, a synonym of getting it.

clue.text: Evil turn makes malignant

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are made into a new word, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A moral comment that turning to evil produces malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'makes' tells you to rearrange EVIL TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something harmful and spreading, as a disease or a hostile attitude.

clue.text: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?

definitions.text: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?

parts.words: Stop on the way to see a Bizet musical drama?
parts.note: reads as halting a journey to watch an opera, but describes a roadside café for drivers, read as an opera title

explanation.surface: Breaking a car journey to catch an opera by Bizet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pull-up is a British roadside transport café, and a carman is a van or lorry driver, so 'carmen' splits into car + men while looking like the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A pull-up is a roadside eating place, and carmen are drivers, so it is a halt for drivers.

clue.text: Type of ground to soak up the moisture

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for soaking is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it so the fibres separate
rain is moisture falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A kind of soil that absorbs water readily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RET (to soak flax, a word mostly met in crosswords) to give TER, followed by RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features, a kind of ground.

clue.text: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on

definitions.text: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on

parts.words: A person one doesn't expect to set eyes on
parts.note: describes a caller who turns up at the door unannounced

explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected guest is someone you had no idea you would see that day.

clue.text: A press organisation that's thin on the ground

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are organised, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper group whose readers are few and far between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like part of the press business, but it signals rearranging A PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is scattered and scanty, few in number over an area.

clue.text: Not bound to deliver

definitions.meaning: not tied up or restrained, at liberty
to release or rescue someone from captivity

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from liberty: unrestrained, and to release a captive.

clue.text: The case for a sewer?

parts.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, not a drain, and the case holds needles

explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and pins used by someone who sews.

clue.text: A custom put to some purpose

definitions.meaning: to employ something for a task

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a habit or practice; as a verb it means to employ.

clue.text: High court judge at Wimbledon

parts.note: sounds like a senior law officer, but is the official sitting in a tall chair on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A senior legal figure attending the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; the official sits on a raised chair beside the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis official rules on play from a high chair, judging on the court.

clue.text: Physical training instructor?

definitions.meaning: done by hand or by bodily effort, as labour
a handbook that teaches how to do or operate something

explanation.surface: A gym coach who leads exercise classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual labour is physical work, and a handbook instructs a learner.

clue.text: Witty cross-talk

parts.note: describes a quick exchange of clever retorts between people

explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is conversation of quick, clever replies traded back and forth.

clue.text: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?

definitions.text: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?

parts.words: Deprived of the advantages of superior birth?
parts.note: describes someone born without wealth or rank, with a hint at a lower berth

explanation.definitionFit: Someone disadvantaged lacks the benefits that come with high social standing.

clue.text: Obsolete European currency unit

parts.note: describes the forerunner of the euro, whose initials name it, and also an old French coin

explanation.definitionFit: The basket currency used in the European Community before the euro is no longer in use.

clue.text: Some haven to which no-one returns

parts.note: a port is a safe harbour

indicators.note: the letters for no and one come back the other way

parts.note: no plus one, with one written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A harbour so remote that nobody ever comes back to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns NO + I into ION, after PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a share or part, as in some of the food.

clue.text: Have to make some acknowledgment

explanation.definitionFit: It means to possess, and also to admit something is true.

clue.text: A detour wrongly announced

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diversion that was badly signposted or described.
explanation.definitionFit: To read out a statement is to say it aloud to listeners, to announce it.

clue.text: The extent to which diets can vary

indicators.note: the letters of the two words change their order, as things that vary do

explanation.surface: How far slimming regimes differ from one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the measure of how far apart things are, their span.

clue.text: Widespread information leading to real trouble

indicators.note: the word for information comes first, leading into the rearranged letters that follow it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are troubled, stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: News that spreads widely and stirs up genuine difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns REAL into ERAL, after GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general is common to most people or places, prevalent.

clue.text: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?

definitions.text: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?

parts.words: Location of a payment that is rightly entered?
parts.note: in bookkeeping, money received goes in the right-hand column of a ledger, so it is entered on the right

explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are recorded in the right-hand column of an account, the side for sums received.

clue.text: A messenger detained outside Burlington House

indicators.note: the word for detained is placed around the abbreviation

parts.note: held means kept in custody
the Royal Academy, RA, is housed in Burlington House in London

explanation.surface: A courier kept waiting outside a London building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts HELD around RA. Burlington House on Piccadilly is home to the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official who carried and proclaimed messages.

clue.text: Move at twice the speed?

parts.note: describes the military pace of ... time, a running step

explanation.definitionFit: To go at the double is to run, moving much faster than a march.

clue.text: Variety of 12 that should ultimately bear fruit

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters take another arrangement

parts.note: refers to the answer at 12 across, the witty cross-talk

explanation.surface: A kind of banter that will pay off in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' signals rearranging the letters of the answer to 12 across. 'Bear fruit' looks figurative but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard tree grows and in time yields pears, its fruit.

clue.text: Simple kind of chair

explanation.definitionFit: It means not hard, and also names a big comfortable armchair.

clue.text: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition

definitions.text: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition

parts.words: Fabulous young victim of soaring ambition
parts.note: fabulous means from fable; a youth of Greek myth flew too near the sun and fell

explanation.definitionFit: The son of Daedalus flew on wax wings, went too high, and plunged into the sea.

clue.text: Amazingly solid East German opera heroine

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are arranged in an amazing new way

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An astonishingly sturdy leading lady from eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' turns SOLID into ISOLD; E follows. 'East German' is a false phrase: East gives E and German belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, a German opera.

clue.text: A turn gone by

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A rotation that has already passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, earlier than now.

clue.text: Not a full-size horse pistol

definitions.meaning: a revolver made by the American firm of that name

explanation.definitionFit: It is a young male horse, and a make of revolver.
